what.text: Bremelanotide, also called PT-141, is a synthetic peptide: a ring-shaped chain of seven amino acids, modelled on a natural hormone called alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone.

src.label: Diamond LE, et al. Int J Impot Res 2004;16(1):51-9
Clayton AH, et al. Clin Ther 2017;39(3):514-526

what.text: It switches on melanocortin receptors, several at once. At the doses studied, the MC1 and MC4 receptors matter most. MC4 receptors sit on nerve cells across the brain. MC1 receptors sit on pigment cells in the skin, which is why it can darken skin. The label says how it works for low sexual desire in women is unknown.

Adonis carries compounded bremelanotide as an oral strip that dissolves on the tongue. It is also an ingredient in Adonis combination products with oxytocin, or with tadalafil and oxytocin, given as a gummy, a tablet or troches.
The only FDA-approved bremelanotide is Vyleesi, an injection under the skin, for premenopausal women. None of the forms Adonis carries is FDA approved, and use in men is off-label.

research.text: Approval rests on two Phase III trials in premenopausal women. In men, the published studies are small early studies run by the developer, Palatin, in 2004 and 2005, and one larger randomized trial from Iran in 2008 that its journal later flagged with an expression of concern. These studies used a nasal spray or injection, not a form taken by mouth.

research.title: Nasal spray, healthy men and men with ED, 2004

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled; two studies reported together; run by Palatin staff
healthy men, and men with mild-to-moderate ED who responded to Viagra. The summary does not give the numbers.
erections measured by a device (RigiScan), drug levels in the blood, side effects

research.found: Erections were greater than with placebo at the higher doses tested. Flushing and nausea were the most common side effects.

src.label: Diamond LE, et al. Int J Impot Res 2004;16(1):51-9

research.title: Injection, men with poor response to Viagra, 2004

facts.v: two studies: rising doses in healthy men, then a placebo-controlled crossover in men with ED
healthy men, and men with ED who had an inadequate response to Viagra. The summary does not give the numbers.
erections measured by RigiScan, with and without erotic video

research.found: Erections were greater than with placebo at both doses tested in the men with ED. The authors described it as well tolerated.

src.label: Rosen RC, et al. Int J Impot Res 2004;16(2):135-42

research.title: Nasal spray plus sildenafil, 2005

facts.v: randomized crossover: low-dose sildenafil plus PT-141, sildenafil plus placebo spray, and placebo plus placebo
19 men with ED who responded to Viagra or Levitra
single doses; erections measured over 6 hours with erotic video
erections by RigiScan, side effects

research.found: The combination produced a greater erection response than sildenafil alone. No new or more frequent side effects were reported.

research.title: Men with ED not helped by sildenafil, 2008 (Iran)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; nasal spray used at home
342 married men aged 28 to 59 with ED who had not responded to sildenafil (172 bremelanotide, 170 placebo)
at least 16 home attempts
International Index of Erectile Function, intercourse satisfaction, side effects

research.found: A positive result was reported in 33.5% on bremelanotide and 8.5% on placebo. More drug-related side effects occurred on bremelanotide. In January 2023 the Journal of Urology published an expression of concern about this paper.

src.label: Safarinejad MR, Hosseini SY. J Urol 2008;179(3):1066-71

research.title: Safety with alcohol, men and women, 2017

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-way crossover; nasal spray
24 healthy adults (12 men, 12 women)
7 days at a research unit
safety, blood pressure, drug levels, with and without alcohol

research.found: No drug interaction with alcohol and no drug-related drops in blood pressure were found. No one left the study for side effects.

src.label: Clayton AH, et al. Clin Ther 2017;39(3):514-526

research.meta: Phase III · began Dec 2014 and Jan 2015 · Two RCTs
research.title: Premenopausal women with low sexual desire (Vyleesi)

facts.v: two identical randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, then a 52-week open-label extension
premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD: 635 on Vyleesi, 632 on placebo; ages 19 to 56
24 weeks, injection used as needed before sex
a sexual desire score and a score for distress about low desire

research.found: Both trials showed statistically significant changes versus placebo. The desire score (range 1.2 to 6) rose 0.5 and 0.6 points on Vyleesi versus 0.2 on placebo; the distress score (range 0 to 4) fell 0.7 versus 0.4. More women stopped early on Vyleesi (40% vs 13%, and 39% vs 25%).

research.text: No study we found tested bremelanotide taken by mouth, as a strip, troche, tablet or gummy.

us.text: Bremelanotide is FDA approved only as Vyleesi, an injection, for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD). It was first approved in 2019. The label says it is not indicated in men or to enhance sexual performance. Use in men is off-label. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: Vyleesi (bremelanotide injection), NDA 210557. Drugs@FDA data show the original approval on June 21, 2019. The label lists initial U.S. approval as 2019.
premenopausal women with low sexual desire that causes marked distress, developed after normal desire, and is not caused by another condition, relationship problems or a drug.
not indicated for HSDD after menopause, in men, or to enhance sexual performance.

world.lead: Outside the US we found no approval of bremelanotide. It has no EU-wide authorisation from EMA and is not on Ireland's list of authorised medicines. Records for Canada, the UK and Australia could not be confirmed.

after.text: Bremelanotide (PT-141) is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. The lists' class S0 bans, at all times, substances not covered by another class that have no current approval by any government health authority for human use. Bremelanotide is approved in the US (Vyleesi), so S0 does not cover it on that basis; WADA has not published a ruling on it.

side.text: Vyleesi's label lists three main warnings: a short rise in blood pressure after each dose, darkening of patches of skin, and nausea. These come from trials in premenopausal women. The small studies in men most often reported flushing and nausea.

items.text: after each dose, blood pressure rose by up to 6 mmHg (top number) and 3 mmHg (bottom number), peaking 2 to 4 hours later, and heart rate fell by up to 5 beats a minute. These usually returned to normal within 12 hours. It is not recommended for people at high risk of heart disease.

patches of darker skin, including on the face, gums and breasts, in 1% of women in the Phase III trials. In another study, 38% developed them after 8 daily doses. Darker skin raised the risk. The darkening did not clearly go away in everyone after stopping.
in 40% of women on Vyleesi, versus 1.3% on placebo. 13% needed anti-nausea medicine and 8% left the trials because of it.
flushing (20.3%), injection-site reactions (13.2%), headache (11.3%) and vomiting (4.8%). 18% stopped because of side effects, versus 2% on placebo. Serious adverse reactions: 1.1% versus 0.5%.
it may slow stomach emptying and so delay or reduce absorption of medicines taken by mouth. It can sharply lower blood levels of oral naltrexone.
animal studies suggest possible harm to a fetus.
flushing and nausea were the most common side effects in early nasal-spray studies, and the 2008 Iranian trial reported more drug-related side effects than placebo. No label describes effects in men.

surprises: PT-141 is widely sold for men, but the only approved product, Vyleesi, carries a label that says it is not indicated in men or to enhance sexual performance.
The largest trial in men (Iran, 2008) is the subject of a 2023 expression of concern from the Journal of Urology.
Vyleesi is an injection. We found no published human study of bremelanotide taken by mouth, as a strip, troche, tablet or gummy.
The label reports skin darkening in 38% of women after 8 daily doses, and it did not clearly reverse in everyone.
